# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01**
**Member:** Sawyer Foster
**Member ID:** W558551284
**Reference Number:** POC-64107D6EF7-65599
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), New Hampshire
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon), effective 11/05/2023 — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield,

I am appealing the denial of my total ankle replacement surgery (CPT 27702), which was denied on 2026-08-01 for "incomplete documentation." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Anthem to reconsider this decision using the medical records already submitted, along with any additional information provided below.

## Why I believe the records support this surgery

The plan's own guideline states that "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met," and lists these requirements: "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved."

Here is how my records address each part of that standard:

**Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.**
My weight-bearing ankle radiographs, taken 2026-06-05, showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. This is the imaging finding the policy asks for.

**Significant pain and functional impairment after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.**
I have had 18 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. During that time I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-03-09 to 2026-06-15, 18 visits), took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16 that gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief. This is more than the 3 months of supervised conservative management the policy requires. I currently walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to about two blocks, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion. [Placeholder: documentation of pain severity on the VAS scale, if available, to be added by treating provider]

**Conservative management components.**
The policy also states that conservative management "should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function," and lists "• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses." My records show NSAID use and a corticosteroid injection, which are two of the listed complementary strategies. [Placeholder: documentation of footwear modification, padding, or orthotic use, if this was tried and not yet included in the submitted records]

**Vascular perfusion and device approval.**
The policy requires "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)" and that the "Device is FDA approved." [Placeholder: vascular exam findings, e.g., pedal pulse documentation, and confirmation that the requested device is FDA-approved, to be supplied by Dr. Okafor's office if not already in the file]

I believe the denial for "incomplete documentation" may be resolved by submitting the additional records noted above, since the core clinical findings — imaging, duration and type of conservative treatment, and functional impairment — appear to already be part of my file and align with the plan's own stated criteria.

## What I am asking

I am requesting that Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield reconsider this denial in light of the records described above and the plan's own medical necessity criteria for ankle arthroplasty. If any specific document is still missing, I would appreciate a clear, itemized list of exactly what is needed so that Dr. Okafor's office and I can provide it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28. I will send this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice, and I understand I may also submit it online through anthem.com or the Sydney Health app, or call the number on my member ID card with questions.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Sawyer Foster
Member ID: W558551284
Date: [date of signing]
Contact phone: [phone number]
Contact address: [mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
